title: Tachycardia with a pulse (adult)
subject: emergency
summary: Unstable tachyarrhythmia (usually 150/min or more with shock, altered mental state, ischaemic pain or acute heart failure) needs synchronised cardioversion under sedation. Stable patients are treated by QRS width and regularity: vagal manoeuvres and adenosine for regular narrow complex, rate control for AF, and antiarrhythmics or elective cardioversion for broad complex.

sections.title: Recognise and classify
items: Rate is typically 150/min or more when the arrhythmia itself causes instability. At lower rates, sinus tachycardia from sepsis, bleeding, hypoxia, pain, PE or thyrotoxicosis is more likely: treat the cause, not the rate.
Instability (AHA): hypotension, acutely altered mental status, signs of shock, ischaemic chest discomfort, acute heart failure. ERC adds syncope and the period immediately after ROSC.
12-lead ECG: narrow (QRS below 0.12 s) or broad (0.12 s or more), regular or irregular.
Treat a regular broad-complex tachycardia as VT until proven otherwise, especially with prior MI or structural heart disease.

sections.title: Unstable: synchronised cardioversion
items: ABC, oxygen if hypoxaemic, monitor, IV access, BP, SpO2; record a rhythm strip during every intervention.
Synchronised cardioversion without delay; sedate or anaesthetise conscious patients (expert help), accepting the risk of haemodynamic worsening.

Energy (AHA 2025): use the device's recommended setting; AF: start at 200 J biphasic or more and escalate; flutter: 200 J may be reasonable; if unknown, use maximum. ERC: AF at maximum output; flutter and SVT 70 to 120 J; VT 120 to 150 J, escalating.
Regular narrow-complex tachycardia: adenosine may be tried while preparing for cardioversion.

If cardioversion fails and instability persists: amiodarone 300 mg IV over 10 to 20 minutes (or procainamide 10 to 15 mg/kg over 20 minutes, maximum 1 g, where available), then repeat cardioversion; follow amiodarone with 900 mg over 24 hours (ERC).
Pulseless VT, or polymorphic VT that cannot be synchronised: unsynchronised defibrillation and the cardiac arrest algorithm.

sections.title: Stable narrow complex
items: Regular (likely AVNRT or AVRT): vagal manoeuvres first. Modified Valsalva: blow into a 10 mL syringe to move the plunger for 15 seconds, then lie flat with legs raised. Avoid carotid massage with a bruit or prior stroke.
Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push into a large proximal vein with a 20 mL saline flush; if no effect, 12 mg. Warn of brief chest discomfort and record the ECG throughout.
Start adenosine at 3 mg via a central line, after heart transplant or with dipyridamole. Avoid in severe asthma or bronchospasm.
Adenosine failure or recurrence: IV verapamil or diltiazem (avoid in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction) or a beta blocker; seek expert advice.

Irregular (probably AF): rate control with a beta blocker or diltiazem. If LVEF is below 40%, use a beta blocker or digoxin; with instability and severely reduced LVEF, digoxin or amiodarone. ERC target heart rate below 110/min.
Do not cardiovert AF electively if it has lasted 48 hours or more (or unknown duration) without anticoagulation or TOE; assess stroke risk and anticoagulate per AF guidance.
Flutter with 2:1 block (ventricular rate about 150/min) is often mistaken for SVT; adenosine may unmask flutter waves but will not terminate it.

sections.title: Stable broad complex
items: Seek expert help. Monomorphic VT with structural heart disease: elective synchronised cardioversion under sedation is often preferred (ERC).

Antiarrhythmics (AHA 2025): amiodarone 150 mg IV over 10 minutes, repeat if VT recurs, then 1 mg/min for 6 hours; or procainamide 20 to 50 mg/min until suppression, hypotension, QRS widening over 50% or 17 mg/kg (avoid with long QT or heart failure). Procainamide is often unavailable in India.
Adenosine only if the broad-complex rhythm is regular and monomorphic (possible SVT with aberrancy); never in irregular or polymorphic broad-complex tachycardia.

Irregular broad complex: AF with bundle branch block, pre-excited AF (WPW) or polymorphic VT. In pre-excited AF avoid AV nodal blockers (adenosine, beta blockers, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin, IV amiodarone); cardiovert if unstable.

Torsades de pointes: magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 10 minutes, correct potassium and magnesium, stop QT-prolonging drugs; defibrillate if pulseless; overdrive pacing or isoprenaline for recurrent pause-dependent torsades (expert).

sections.title: Investigations
items: 12-lead ECG before and after conversion (pre-excitation, QT, ischaemia).
Potassium, magnesium, calcium, glucose, renal function, TSH, troponin if ischaemia suspected, blood gas; echocardiography.
Drug history: QT-prolonging drugs, digoxin, stimulants, thyroxine, salbutamol.

sections.title: Disposition
items: SVT terminated, normal ECG, no structural disease: usually discharge with vagal manoeuvre teaching and cardiology referral (catheter ablation is curative).
Admit VT, pre-excitation, AF or flutter with instability, recurrent arrhythmia, or any arrhythmia with ischaemia or heart failure to a monitored bed.
After cardioversion for AF or flutter, continue anticoagulation for at least 4 weeks, then according to long-term stroke risk.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Rate-control drugs for compensatory sinus tachycardia (sepsis, bleeding, PE).
Verapamil or diltiazem for a broad-complex tachycardia assumed to be SVT: can cause collapse if it is VT.
Forgetting sync mode, or not re-selecting sync after each shock on devices that reset.
Slow adenosine injection through a small hand vein (drug is metabolised before reaching the heart).

drugs.name: Adenosine
drugs.dose: 6 mg rapid IV push with 20 mL saline flush; 12 mg if no effect
drugs.notes: 3 mg via central line, after heart transplant or with dipyridamole. Regular rhythms only.

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.dose: Stable VT (AHA): 150 mg IV over 10 minutes, repeat if needed, then 1 mg/min for 6 hours. Failed cardioversion (ERC): 300 mg IV over 10 to 20 minutes, then 900 mg over 24 hours
drugs.notes: Give via a large or central vein; watch for hypotension and bradycardia.

drugs.name: Procainamide
drugs.dose: 20 to 50 mg/min IV until arrhythmia suppressed, hypotension, QRS widens over 50% or 17 mg/kg given; maintenance 1 to 4 mg/min
drugs.notes: Avoid with prolonged QT or heart failure. Limited availability in India.

drugs.name: Diltiazem
drugs.dose: 0.25 mg/kg IV over 2 minutes (usually 15 to 20 mg); if needed after 15 minutes, 0.35 mg/kg (20 to 25 mg)
drugs.notes: Rate control of AF or flutter, or SVT after adenosine. Avoid in HFrEF, hypotension and pre-excitation.

drugs.name: Metoprolol
drugs.dose: 2.5 to 5 mg IV over 2 minutes, repeated every 5 to 10 minutes to a maximum of 15 mg
drugs.notes: Avoid in acute decompensated heart failure, severe asthma and pre-excitation.
